questions.prompt: Although you had loved that city greatly, you abandoned it in the war.
questions.answer: Quamquam illam urbem magnopere amārās, eam in bellō relīquistī.

questions.prompt: The soldiers destroyed the walls which the enemy had built with great labor.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs mūrōs, quōs hostēs magnō labōre exstrūxerant, dēlērunt.

questions.prompt: They say that you praised the poet whose verses you had never read.
questions.answer: Dīcunt tē poētam laudāsse cuius versūs numquam lēgerās.

questions.prompt: When you had freed the captives, the whole city rejoiced.
questions.answer: Cum captīvōs līberāssēs, tōta urbs gāvīsa est.

questions.prompt: Tell me the truth about the crime, my friend.
questions.answer: Dīc mihi vērum dē scelere, amīce.

questions.prompt: Do what the laws command, and fear nothing.
questions.answer: Fac quod lēgēs iubent, et nihil timē.

questions.prompt: Finish the work you began, and lead out the army.
questions.answer: Cōnfice opus quod coepistī, et exercitum ēdūc.

questions.prompt: You know that these barbarians have provoked us with great contempt.
questions.answer: Nōstī hōs barbarōs magnō contemptū nōs prōvocāsse.

questions.prompt: You heard the truth from a wounded and unarmed messenger.
questions.answer: Vērum ā nūntiō vulnerātō atque inermī audīstī.

questions.prompt: They had loved their homeland so much that they preferred to die.
questions.answer: Patriam adeō amārant ut morī māllent.

questions.prompt: Lead your army across the river, general, and conquer the barbarians.
questions.answer: Dūc exercitum tuum trāns flūmen, dux, et barbarōs vince.

questions.prompt: Do this at once, and tell me nothing about the crime.
questions.answer: Fac hoc statim, et nihil mihi dē scelere dīc.

questions.prompt: Lead out the troops from the camp and finish the work before dawn.
questions.answer: Ēdūc cōpiās ē castrīs et opus ante lūcem cōnfice.

questions.prompt: Say the truth to the king, or lead these captives to death.
questions.answer: Dīc rēgī vērum, aut hōs captīvōs ad mortem dūc.

questions.prompt: You have often praised those poets whom you never once heard.
questions.answer: Saepe illōs poētās laudāstī quōs numquam audīstī.

questions.prompt: The enemy destroyed the walls which our ancestors had built with great toil.
questions.answer: Hostēs mūrōs dēlērunt quōs maiōrēs nostrī magnō labōre exstrūxerant.

questions.prompt: I know that you have long loved that maiden with a faithful heart.
questions.answer: Sciō tē illam virginem fidēlī animō diū amāsse.

questions.prompt: If you had known the truth, you would have kept silent.
